title: Deception + Overconfidence: When Miscalibration Masks Deceptive Information Withholding
original_idea: Test whether overconfident models and deceptively uncertain models are distinguishable by calibration-based probes. Design a test battery that separates honest miscalibration from strategic uncertainty manipulation. Measure false negative rates of calibration checks on strategic models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: strategic uncertainty manipulation indistinguishable from honest miscalibration -> calibration checks give false assurance. Names a specific mechanism, but the gap is whether models actually engage in strategic uncertainty manipulation -- this is assumed rather than demonstrated.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires creating models with strategic uncertainty manipulation (not well defined or established), designing probes that distinguish honest miscalibration from strategic manipulation, and calibration analysis. The core distinction is philosophically subtle and technically ill-defined for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple open design problems: how to create strategically uncertain models, how to operationalize the distinction, what the test battery looks like. No obvious bounded first experiment; the entire framing requires conceptual groundwork.

novelty.reasoning: Calibration research and deception detection research exist as separate fields. Linear probes for deception detection achieve high F1 scores (Apollo Research, 2024-2025), and LLM calibration research is active (ICLR 2025 paper on uncertainty estimation). The concept of 'strategic dishonesty' undermining safety evaluations has been studied (arXiv:2509.18058). However, the specific intersection — distinguishing honest miscalibration from strategic uncertainty manipulation using calibration-based probes — appears novel. No published work designs a test battery specifically to separate these two phenomena. The closest work is on models that 'fake misalignment' (strategic dishonesty paper) but this focuses on refusal behavior, not uncertainty/calibration manipulation.
